title: Adam Smith and Classical Economics
text: Adam Smith (1723–1790) was a Scottish economist and moral philosopher widely considered the father of modern economics. His major work, The Wealth of Nations (1776), laid the foundations of classical free market economic theory. Smith introduced the concept of the invisible hand — the idea that individuals pursuing their own self-interest in free markets tend to promote the general good of society. He analyzed the division of labor and its role in increasing productivity using the famous pin factory example. Smith advocated for free trade, limited government intervention in the economy, and criticized monopolies and mercantilist policies. His work influenced generations of economists and policymakers.
